title: Career Roadmap — Film Editor
summary: A Film Editor transforms recorded footage into a coherent, engaging visual story. The role involves selecting takes, arranging scenes, refining pacing, synchronising sound, maintaining continuity and collaborating with directors and post-production teams.

about.label: Career domain
about.text: Film Production, Post-Production, Television, OTT & Digital Media

blocks.text: A Film Editor transforms recorded footage into a coherent, engaging visual story. The role involves selecting takes, arranging scenes, refining pacing, synchronising sound, maintaining continuity and collaborating with directors and post-production teams.
Key responsibilities

items.text: Select shots and assemble scenes according to the script and director's vision.
Manage continuity, pacing, rhythm and storytelling.
Synchronise dialogue, music and sound effects.
Coordinate with colourists, sound designers, VFX artists and directors.
Export final cuts in the required formats and technical specifications.

blocks.text: This roadmap assumes a four-year undergraduate programme. For a three-year degree, combine the later milestones.

rows.text: Film language, shot composition, storytelling, continuity and basic editing
Edit three short videos and a 60-second montage
Narrative editing, transitions, sound synchronisation, pacing and colour fundamentals
Advanced editing, multicamera footage, proxies, sound workflows and internships
Edit a short film or documentary with a production team
Professional post-production workflows, showreel development and industry networking
Build a professional showreel and complete a portfolio project
Exposure, white balance, contrast and colour matching
Dialogue cleanup, sound effects, music and mixing
Titles, lower thirds and animated graphics
File naming, backups, codecs and export settings
Emotional pacing, scene transitions and narrative clarity
Feedback, version control and director communication
Shared review tools and production workflows

blocks.label: Recommended starting point
blocks.text: DaVinci Resolve offers a capable free version and combines editing, colour correction, audio post-production and visual effects tools. Start with one editing application before investing in multiple subscriptions.
Complete at least five projects during the degree.

blocks.label: Continuity edit
blocks.text: Assemble footage into a coherent scene with consistent screen direction.

blocks.label: Short narrative film
blocks.text: Edit a 3–5-minute story with clear pacing and emotional progression.

blocks.label: Documentary sequence
blocks.text: Combine interviews, B-roll, narration and music.

blocks.label: Music or promotional video
blocks.text: Demonstrate rhythm, visual matching and beat-based editing.

blocks.label: Before-and-after edit
blocks.text: Show the raw footage, rough cut and final edit, explaining your editorial decisions.
For each project, document your role, editing software, footage source, deliverables and challenges. Use licensed, self-shot or otherwise authorised footage.

Verify current vacancies, eligibility, stipends and deadlines directly with the organisation.

blocks.label: Official learning resources
blocks.text: Blackmagic Design Training, Adobe Learn and Avid.
Certificates can help structure learning, but a strong showreel and reliable editing workflow are generally more useful evidence of ability.
Entry level
Editing Intern · Assistant Film Editor · Junior Video Editor · Post-Production Assistant
Mid-career
Film Editor · Documentary Editor · Television Editor · Senior Video Editor
Senior and leadership
Senior Film Editor · Supervising Editor · Post-Production Supervisor · Post-Production Director
Adjacent career options include colourist, assistant editor, motion graphics artist, sound editor, VFX editor and post-production producer.
Progression depends on portfolio quality, project credits, technical reliability, creative judgement and professional relationships. Many editors work freelance or on a project basis.

blocks.text: Check current course availability, entrance requirements, portfolio expectations, equipment access and fees through official admissions pages.
A postgraduate qualification is not universally necessary for film editing. Practical experience and a demonstrable showreel can provide alternative entry routes.
Potential destinations include the USA, UK, Canada, Australia and New Zealand. Relevant programmes include film editing, post-production, film production and digital cinema.
Before applying, verify tuition, scholarships, programme prerequisites, work authorisation and access to industry placements. An international qualification does not guarantee employment.

rows.text: Learn editing fundamentals, complete projects and build a showreel
Work on varied productions and develop a specialisation
Lead editing projects and collaborate with directors and post-production teams
Progress toward supervising editing, post-production leadership or an independent editing business

blocks.text: These are illustrative planning horizons, not guaranteed promotion dates.
